video_title: Micah Nori Media Availability | 2026 Training Camp, Day 3 | Portland Trail Blazers

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on Scoot Henderson's development and playing with pace
quotes.excerpt: the thing that we're trying to do with Scoot is continue to play with pace
quotes.quote: The thing that we're trying to do with Scoot is continue to play with pace. The things I just tell him is just go as fast as you can. If somebody's in front of you, pass it. If they don't, just lay the ball in. Just simplify his game. I think that Scoot to me is more of a combo type guy than just a true point guard, and I think he would agree with that. So I told him I don't need you to worry about everybody else as far as facilitating and orchestrating. We will get stuff off of you just pushing pace and being who you are.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says the Blazers are simplifying Scoot Henderson's role by encouraging him to play with pace rather than acting as a traditional point guard. Nori believes Scoot is more of a combo guard who should focus on attacking the paint.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori compares Scoot Henderson's playstyle to Russell Westbrook
quotes.excerpt: I kind of look at him as a Russell Westbrook type player
quotes.quote: I kind of look at him as a Russell Westbrook type player where he can be very dominant on both sides of the floor. He can also impact the glass. He's a strong, athletic guy and just that's how you want him to play when he's on the ball. Just play with pace, attack gaps, attack the paint, kick out from there. Make sure you get your finishing, and I think that's what we're looking for.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori sees a Russell Westbrook type player in Scoot Henderson. Nori wants Scoot to leverage his athleticism to dominate on both ends of the floor, impact the glass, and attack gaps to create opportunities for himself and teammates.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori discusses Scoot Henderson's injury history and development
quotes.excerpt: I feel bad for Scoot because we've missed him quite a bit with the injuries
quotes.quote: I feel bad for Scoot because we've missed him quite a bit with the injuries. But the one thing that I see with Scoot when I've seen is he kind of would get himself in trouble when he ends up playing in a little bit of a crowd and playing a little bit too fast for himself. But at the end of the day, I have seen nothing since I've been here, and I'm not just saying this, but it's been good Scoot. It really has been, just at both ends of the floor asking him to be aggressive defensively, get into the ball, blow some things up, and he's trying to do that.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori says he has seen nothing but good things from Scoot Henderson during training camp. Nori is pushing Scoot to be more aggressive defensively and avoid playing too fast when he gets into crowds.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on the importance of brutal truths in coaching
quotes.excerpt: we talked about it on the first day of the slideshow, just brutal truths
quotes.quote: We talked about it on the first day of the slideshow, just brutal truths. And I think if you just, I think in anything we're doing, like I tell them, yeah, it's an open-door policy, but instead of letting things fester, all of a sudden something that just may be a speed bump, don't turn that into a mountain by letting it just you're worrying. I think these conversations, and it's not just, I think we can all relate to it, that you always worry about having a conversation. But then when you have the conversation, like, oh, that went a lot better than what I thought.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori is emphasizing brutal truths and open communication with his players this season. Nori wants to address issues immediately rather than letting them fester into larger problems.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori on his coaching philosophy and staff involvement
quotes.excerpt: our coaches will coach and I'm not running every single drill
quotes.quote: In our practices, our coaches will coach and I'm not running every single drill. I'm not the only voice they hear because I think that there is a shelf life to your voice and just constantly, you end up, I always joke, you sound like Charlie Brown's teacher after a while. That's what we don't want. And then you just try and pick and choose your spots, and I think that hopefully by again, letting them know what's expected, holding them to that standard and holding them accountable to it, so when you do get on them, then they are like, oh yeah, that makes sense.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori is intentionally diversifying the voices in practice to avoid having a limited shelf life with his players. He says he is not running every drill because he does not want to sound like Charlie Brown's teacher.

quotes.speaker: Micah Nori
quotes.summary_phrase: Micah Nori outlines the coaching staff responsibilities
quotes.excerpt: Quinton Crawford is running the defense and then Jay is doing the offense
quotes.quote: Quinton Crawford is running the defense and then Jay is doing the offense. Mike Williams, who is my number two, is doing all special situations and late game stuff and helping like rotations and all that. And then what Mike is doing, Mike is still a young coach as is Q, but Mike is great on both sides of the ball. And so what I have him doing is not to necessarily pigeonhole him, but he's helping Jay when we split up stuff and we do two offensive stations, he'll take one while Q's got a defense and then vice versa. So it's a nice mix and a nice flow.
quotes.social_post: Micah Nori detailed his coaching staff roles. Quinton Crawford is running the defense, Jay is handling the offense, and Mike Williams is managing special situations and late game rotations.
